acceptance: adapter.load_data on an iceberg manifest loads all 8 TPC-H tables at SF0.01 with row counts and per-column checksums equal to the native CSV load
a unit test registers a real converter-written Iceberg directory
context: Related done item perf-duckdb-wire-native-handlers-20261030. Not fixed by the verifier.
description:
Found by live verification of #3950 (perf-duckdb-wire-native-handlers-20261030) on origin/develop 525361b2f8, duckdb with pyiceberg from the table-formats extra.

Reproduction: generate TPC-H SF0.01 with the iceberg converter (`benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01 --table-format iceberg --phases generate`), then load through the adapter: DuckDBAdapter(database_path=...), adapter.requested_table_format='iceberg', create_schema, load_data(benchmark, conn, <data dir>) (script /tmp/lv/dd_direct.py iceberg ...).
Expected: 8 tables load with dbgen row counts (customer 1500, lineitem 60175, ...).
Actual: every table prints `Failed to bulk-load <table>: Namespace does not exist: benchbox` and the returned stats are 0 for all 8 tables (/tmp/live-verify-dd-iceberg-direct.log). A second defect sits behind the first: IcebergFileHandler.load_table (benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py) calls catalog.register_table(('benchbox', table), str(file_path)) with the table DIRECTORY; pyiceberg needs a *.metadata.json location and raises `OSError: Cannot open for reading: path ... is a directory` (verified separately; registering the latest metadata.json gives 1500 customer rows). Before #3950 the directory was rejected earlier (DataLoadingError 'shard path is a directory with no data files'), so the Iceberg route never worked end to end on DuckDB.

What does work: the #3950 Arrow insert itself. insert_arrow_table on Arrow tables read from the same Iceberg tables via pyiceberg StaticTable inserts all 8 tables with row count and per-column checksum parity against a native CSV load (/tmp/live-verify-dd-direct-parity.log). Vortex (DuckDB-extension-written and Python-bindings-written files, handler DuckDBVortexHandler, no fallback needed) and DuckLake (metadata.ducklake directories) both pass parity.

Note: the CLI path `--platform duckdb --table-format iceberg|vortex` does not exercise these handlers at all: it converts the files but loads the .tbl shards (log says 'from 10 shard(s)'), so a CLI run cannot show Iceberg/Vortex load correctness.

Suspected symbol: IcebergFileHandler.load_table in benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py (create namespace with catalog.create_namespace_if_not_exists, register the highest-numbered metadata/*.metadata.json).
